subject: Rendering a table in latex when a rowname starts with [

messages.author: 2ed8fbee6778722d
messages.subject: Rendering a table in latex when a rowname starts with [
parts:
Dear all,

I am using knitr to produce PDF documents using pdflatex. I have to print a table which has chemical names as its rownames. One rowname starts with left square bracket [. I am trying to include this table in my knitr document using print(xtable(tab)), but latex fails to render this. Below I create a toy example to describe the issue. The following document doesn't render.


\documentclass{article}

egin{document}

<<results='asis'>>=
tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
rownames(tab) <- c("a", "[b]c")
colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")
library(xtable)
print(xtable(tab))
@

\end{document}

One dirty workaround I found was to insert a line change character at the beginning of the rowname that starts with [. That is, the following document renders correctly:


\documentclass{article}

egin{document}

<<results='asis'>>=
tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
rownames(tab) <- c("a", " [b]c")
colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")
library(xtable)
print(xtable(tab))
@

\end{document}

Therefore, in my real case the knitr code using this workaround is something like the following (which is just a generalization of the above by inserting wherever needed):

\documentclass{article}

egin{document}

<<results='asis'>>=
tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
rownames(tab) <- c("a", "[b]c")
colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")

### I insert at the beginning of rownames that start with [
rownames(tab) <- gsub("^\[", " \[", rownames(tab))
library(xtable)
print(xtable(tab))
@
\end{document}

I tried to achieve this same workaround using sanitize.rownames.function as below (because I think that it is a slightly less dirty way of doing the same thing, as it wouldn't change the rownames permanently):

\documentclass{article}

egin{document}

<<results='asis'>>=
tab <- matrix(rnorm(4), nrow=2)
rownames(tab) <- c("a", "[b]c")
colnames(tab) <- c("p", "q")

library(xtable)
print(xtable(tab),
  sanitize.rownames.function=function(x) { gsub("^\[", " \[", x) }
)
@
\end{document}

So, my questions are:

1. Is there a more elegant way (or a more automatic way) of solving this issue?
2. If my workaround is reasonable, how should I fix my sanitize.rownames.function?

Thanks a lot in advance.

Best regards,
Gopal

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Rendering a table in latex when a rowname starts with [
parts:
It is probably an xtable bug. I just tested knitr::kable(), and it did
not have the problem:

library(knitr)
kable(tab)
@

\end{document}

I guess the best way to solve the problem is to ask xtable authors to
fix it. You can also set your sanitize.rownames.function as a global
option in R via options(), though.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name
